The skill requires grounding the visual read in the evaluation narrative and metrics, so I’m now tracing the supplied parent guidance, sampled result, inherited notes, and rollout artifacts; I’ll inspect both prewarm and wake keyframes before proposing any controller change.

The keyframes show the seed does not enter the useful wake corridor: after release it quickly rotates nose-down, translates mostly downward, crosses the lower boundary, and leaves after only 50.1 time units. That visual diagnosis matches the tiny net target progress (0.024), large downward displacement (−13.30L), negative mean local vertical flow, and high moment/command effort. I’m checking the actual state/API contract and inherited policy logs next so the replacement uses only available normalized body-frame feedback.

I’m recording that limitation explicitly. The candidate hypothesis will preserve the seed’s demonstrated upstream displacement while adding a bounded, target-bearing-dependent curvature center; its key falsifier is whether bearing shrinks before the previous downward exit develops.

The single candidate and both required evidence files are now updated. The durable lesson records a concrete negative result from the seed—upstream motion was overwhelmed by lateral escape—and gives a falsification boundary for bearing correction. This is not a policy or evidence failure. Per the runner’s “repair and rerun” instruction, I’m removing only the duplicate parent listing, then rerunning the unchanged checker.
